question: By whom does Paul declare he was commissioned as an apostle in Galatians 1:1, explicitly denying human origin?
opt1: Not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead
opt2: By the ecclesiastical council of the twelve apostles residing in Jerusalem
opt3: Through formal imperial appointment granted by the proconsul of Galatia
opt4: By the democratic election of the local congregations throughout Asia Minor
correct: Not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead
explanation: Paul immediately asserts his divine apostolic commission directly from the risen Christ and God the Father without human intermediary. Galatians 1:1 (KJV) - "Paul, an apostle, (not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead;)"

question: For what great purpose did our Lord Jesus Christ give Himself for our sins according to Galatians 1:4?
opt1: That believers might establish a temporal earthly kingdom dominating pagan nations
opt2: That he might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father
opt3: That mankind might achieve philosophical enlightenment through ascetic contemplation
opt4: That all ceremonial dietary washings of the Levitical code might be enforced globally
correct: That he might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father
explanation: Christ's sacrificial atonement rescues redeemed believers from the corrupt moral system and tyranny of this fallen age. Galatians 1:4 (KJV) - "Who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father:"

question: Why was Paul astonished concerning the sudden spiritual deflection of the Galatian believers in Galatians 1:6?
opt1: That they had completely ceased attending public assemblies in the cities
opt2: That they had refused to pay taxes to the Roman provincial authorities
opt3: That ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel
opt4: That they had forgotten the Greek language and adopted barbarian customs
correct: That ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel
explanation: Paul expressed deep grief that the Galatians were rapidly abandoning the gospel of free grace for a legalistic counterfeit. Galatians 1:6 (KJV) - "I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel:"

question: What solemn apostolic anathema does Paul pronounce upon anyone preaching any other gospel than what he preached?
opt1: Let him be fined thirty pieces of silver by the municipal court
opt2: Let him be sent to the school of Alexandria for corrective instruction
opt3: Let his books be publicly sealed until the arrival of the Jerusalem elders
opt4: Though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed
correct: Though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed
explanation: The purity of the apostolic gospel is inviolable: any distortion brings divine curse (anathema), even if delivered by an angel. Galatians 1:8 (KJV) - "But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed."

question: What question does Paul pose in Galatians 1:10 regarding his motive in gospel ministry?
opt1: For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ
opt2: Do I demand personal tithes from the poor, or do I distribute my private wealth to the needy?
opt3: Have I compromised the truth to escape imprisonment, or have I courted persecution voluntarily?
opt4: Did I seek letters of commendation from the high priest, or did I preach without ecclesiastical authority?
correct: For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ
explanation: Paul declares that seeking human popularity or cultural approval is entirely incompatible with being a true servant of Jesus Christ. Galatians 1:10 (KJV) - "For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ."

question: How did Paul receive the gospel which he preached according to Galatians 1:11-12?
opt1: Through private tutorials conducted by the senior apostles in Capernaum
opt2: For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ
opt3: From ancient rabbinic scrolls preserved in the library of Gamaliel
opt4: By synthesizing Greek philosophical logic with the Hebrew prophets
correct: For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ
explanation: Paul's gospel message was neither a human tradition nor acquired through human pedagogy, but revealed directly by Jesus Christ. Galatians 1:12 (KJV) - "For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ."

question: How had Paul formerly conducted himself in the Jews' religion prior to his conversion in Galatians 1:13?
opt1: He served as a peaceful scribe translating the Septuagint into Greek
opt2: He withdrew to the desert community of the Essenes near the Salt Sea
opt3: Beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it
opt4: He advocated religious tolerance and dialogue between Pharisees and Sadducees
correct: Beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it
explanation: Paul reminds the Galatians of his former fanatical zeal, ruthlessly persecuting and attempting to devastate the church of God. Galatians 1:13 (KJV) - "For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews' religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:"

question: To whom did God reveal His Son in Paul, and what was the divine purpose in Galatians 1:15-16?
opt1: To make him the chief ruler over the Sanhedrin in Jerusalem
opt2: To authorize him to collect temple taxes throughout the Roman empire
opt3: To command him to rebuild the physical temple on Mount Gerizim
opt4: To reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the heathen; immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood
correct: To reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the heathen; immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood
explanation: God sovereignly set Paul apart from birth to reveal Christ in him so that he would become the apostle to the Gentiles. Galatians 1:16 (KJV) - "To reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the heathen; immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood:"

question: Whither did Paul go immediately after his conversion, instead of going up to Jerusalem in Galatians 1:17?
opt1: I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus
opt2: I sailed directly to Rome to preach before the imperial senate
opt3: I journeyed into Egypt to study in the libraries of Alexandria
opt4: I retreated to the island of Cyprus with Barnabas and Mark
correct: I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus
explanation: Paul spent time in Arabia in direct communion with God before returning to Damascus, demonstrating his independence from Jerusalem. Galatians 1:17 (KJV) - "Neither went I up to Jerusalem to them which were apostles before me; but I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus."

question: Whom did Paul visit in Jerusalem after three years, and how long did he abide with him in Galatians 1:18?
opt1: He visited the high priest Caiaphas and lodged with him forty days
opt2: I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days
opt3: He met with the seven deacons and stayed with them for six months
opt4: He conferred with Apollos and Silas for an entire sabbatical year
correct: I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days
explanation: After three years in Arabia and Damascus, Paul made a brief fifteen-day visit to Peter, seeing only James the Lord's brother. Galatians 1:18 (KJV) - "Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days."

question: Who accompanied Paul when he went up again to Jerusalem fourteen years later in Galatians 2:1?
opt1: He traveled alone in disguise to escape Jewish pursuers
opt2: He was escorted by a Roman centurion and twenty soldiers
opt3: I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also
opt4: He journeyed exclusively with Silas and Timothy from Antioch
correct: I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also
explanation: Fourteen years after his previous visit, Paul returned to Jerusalem with Barnabas, intentionally bringing uncircumcised Titus. Galatians 2:1 (KJV) - "Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also."

question: Was Titus, who was with Paul, being a Greek, compelled to be circumcised in Jerusalem in Galatians 2:3?
opt1: Yes, he was circumcised publicly to satisfy the elders of Judea
opt2: He submitted to circumcision voluntarily to preach in synagogues
opt3: He was required to undergo ceremonial purification at the temple
opt4: But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised
correct: But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised
explanation: The Jerusalem leadership refused to compel Titus to be circumcised, vindicating the principle of Gentile Christian freedom. Galatians 2:3 (KJV) - "But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised:"

question: Why were false brethren secretly brought into the assembly according to Galatians 2:4?
opt1: Who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage
opt2: To collect voluntary donations for the impoverished saints of Galilee
opt3: To record the genealogies of Gentile converts for civil archives
opt4: To negotiate commercial treaties between Antioch and Jerusalem
correct: Who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage
explanation: Judaizing infiltrators sought to undermine the liberty believers possess in Christ and impose the yoke of the ceremonial law. Galatians 2:4 (KJV) - "And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage:"

question: How did the apostles perceive the division of missionary stewardship between Peter and Paul in Galatians 2:7?
opt1: Peter was made absolute bishop over all churches worldwide
opt2: The gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter
opt3: Paul was restricted to preaching only in the province of Cilicia
opt4: Both apostles were commanded to cease evangelizing outside Judea
correct: The gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter
explanation: God sovereignly apportioned their apostolic callings: Peter primarily to the Jews, and Paul primarily to the Gentile nations. Galatians 2:7 (KJV) - "But contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter;"

question: Which three leaders who seemed to be pillars gave to Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship?
opt1: Stephen, Philip, and Prochorus the deacons
opt2: Nicodemus, Joseph of Arimathaea, and Gamaliel
opt3: James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars
opt4: Matthias, Bartholomew, and Thomas the apostles
correct: James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars
explanation: James, Peter (Cephas), and John recognized God's grace upon Paul and officially confirmed mutual fellowship in gospel partnership. Galatians 2:9 (KJV) - "And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision."

question: What single charitable request did the Jerusalem pillars make of Paul and Barnabas in Galatians 2:10?
opt1: That they should send annual tithes to the temple treasury
opt2: That all Gentile converts should observe the feast of Tabernacles
opt3: That they should ordain only Levites to pastoral ministry
opt4: Only they would that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do
correct: Only they would that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do
explanation: The sole practical request from Jerusalem was continued charitable care for the poor saints, which Paul zealously pursued. Galatians 2:10 (KJV) - "Only they would that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do."

question: Why did Paul publicly withstand Peter to the face at Antioch in Galatians 2:11-12?
opt1: Because he was to be blamed. For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself
opt2: Because Peter demanded personal financial payment for visiting the church
opt3: Because Peter refused to ordain Barnabas as an apostle of the Gentiles
opt4: Because Peter denied the bodily resurrection of the Lord Jesus Christ
correct: Because he was to be blamed. For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself
explanation: Peter compromised the gospel of grace by withdrawing from table fellowship with Gentile believers out of fear of the circumcision party. Galatians 2:11-12 (KJV) - "But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision."

question: What foundational doctrine of justification does Paul articulate in Galatians 2:16?
opt1: Justification is attained by combining faith with ceremonial washings
opt2: A man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ... for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified
opt3: Righteousness is imputed exclusively through natural moral excellence
opt4: The law justifies the circumcised, while faith justifies the uncircumcised
correct: A man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ... for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified
explanation: Salvation is by faith in Christ alone; legalistic obedience to Mosaic commandments cannot justify any human being before God. Galatians 2:16 (KJV) - "Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified."

question: What profound confession of identification with Christ does Paul make in Galatians 2:20?
opt1: I fulfill all the commandments of Moses and am found blameless under the covenant
opt2: I seek mystical union with angelic powers through strict ascetic vigils
opt3: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me
opt4: I boast in my ancestral lineage and rabbinic ordination before the Sanhedrin
correct: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me
explanation: The Christian's old self is co-crucified with Christ, and the new life is animated by the indwelling Christ through faith. Galatians 2:20 (KJV) - "I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me."

question: What devastating conclusion follows if righteousness could come through the law according to Galatians 2:21?
opt1: Then the Gentile converts must immediately build a temple
opt2: Then Abraham's faith was merely an allegorical myth
opt3: Then the Holy Spirit is confined exclusively to Jerusalem
opt4: If righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain
correct: If righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain
explanation: To seek justification through the law nullifies God's grace and implies that the substitutionary death of Christ was utterly superfluous. Galatians 2:21 (KJV) - "I do not frustrate the grace of God: for if righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain."

question: With what piercing question does Paul address the Galatians at the beginning of Chapter 3?
opt1: O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you?
opt2: O noble Galatians, why have ye neglected the daily burnt offerings prescribed by Moses?
opt3: O prudent Galatians, which of the Greek philosophers taught you to abandon wisdom?
opt4: O faithful Galatians, have ye received the imperial decree commanding public sacrifice?
correct: O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you?
explanation: Paul forcefully rebukes their spiritual folly, as if under a spell, for abandoning the vividly portrayed truth of Christ crucified. Galatians 3:1 (KJV) - "O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you?"

question: What diagnostic inquiry regarding the Holy Spirit does Paul ask the Galatians in Galatians 3:2?
opt1: Did ye receive the Spirit through formal circumcision performed by a priest?
opt2: Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?
opt3: Did ye purchase the gift of the Holy Spirit with gold and silver in Antioch?
opt4: Was the Spirit imparted unto you by the civil magistrates of the province?
correct: Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?
explanation: Their own spiritual experience proved the gospel: they received the Holy Spirit through believing the message of faith, not by legal works. Galatians 3:2 (KJV) - "This only would I learn of you, Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?"

question: Who are declared to be the true children of Abraham in Galatians 3:7?
opt1: Those who can trace biological lineage to the twelve sons of Jacob
opt2: Those who observe all annual feast days in the temple of Jerusalem
opt3: Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham
opt4: Those who possess land inheritances in the mountains of Judea
correct: Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham
explanation: True spiritual descent from Abraham is defined not by physical genealogy, but by sharing the patriarch's justifying faith in God. Galatians 3:7 (KJV) - "Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham."

question: What ancient gospel promise made to Abraham did the Scripture foresee concerning the Gentiles in Galatians 3:8?
opt1: Thy biological seed shall conquer all earthly empires by the sword
opt2: Thou shalt erect an altar of unhewn stones in every pagan capital
opt3: Thy descendants shall enforce circumcision upon all barbarian tribes
opt4: In thee shall all nations be blessed
correct: In thee shall all nations be blessed
explanation: Centuries before the law, God preached the gospel to Abraham, promising universal blessing to all nations through faith. Galatians 3:8 (KJV) - "And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed."

question: Why are all who rely on the works of the law under a curse according to Galatians 3:10?
opt1: For it is written, Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them
opt2: Because the ceremonial law was originally delivered by fallen angels
opt3: Because Moses failed to write down all commandments with sufficient clarity
opt4: Because the law was intended only for the first generation in the wilderness
correct: For it is written, Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them
explanation: The law demands absolute, unbroken obedience; failing in any single commandment places the sinner under divine condemnation. Galatians 3:10 (KJV) - "For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them."

question: What OT passage from Habakkuk 2:4 proves that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God?
opt1: The soul that sinneth, it shall die
opt2: The just shall live by faith
opt3: Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand
opt4: He that doeth them shall live in them
correct: The just shall live by faith
explanation: Habakkuk 2:4 definitively demonstrates that true life and righteousness before God have always been received through faith alone. Galatians 3:11 (KJV) - "But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith."

question: How did Christ redeem us from the curse of the law according to Galatians 3:13?
opt1: By paying monetary tribute to the high priest and the Roman senate
opt2: By abolishing the moral requirements of holiness in the universe
opt3: Being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree
opt4: By establishing an earthly military dynasty in the city of David
correct: Being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree
explanation: Christ endured the penal curse of divine judgment in our place on the cross, liberating us forever from the law's condemnation. Galatians 3:13 (KJV) - "Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree:"

question: To whom does Paul explain that the promise to Abraham's 'seed' specifically referred in Galatians 3:16?
opt1: It referred to the entire biological nation of Israel throughout history
opt2: It referred to the seventy elders who assembled under Moses in Sinai
opt3: It referred to the kings who sat upon the royal throne of Judah
opt4: He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ
correct: He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ
explanation: Paul highlights the singular form 'seed' to show that the covenant promises find their ultimate fulfillment in Jesus Christ. Galatians 3:16 (KJV) - "Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ."

question: What was the purpose of the Mosaic law in relation to Christ according to Galatians 3:24?
opt1: Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith
opt2: The law was given as a permanent rival to the gospel of grace for salvation
opt3: The law was intended to replace Abraham's covenant with an eternal legal code
opt4: The law was designed to grant spiritual perfection through ritual sacrifices
correct: Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith
explanation: The law served as a strict guardian (paidagogos) exposing our guilt and helplessness to guide us to justification in Christ. Galatians 3:24 (KJV) - "Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith."

question: What revolutionary equality and unity exists among all believers baptized into Christ in Galatians 3:28?
opt1: All social and economic classes are dissolved into a political commune
opt2: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus
opt3: Only freeborn Jewish men may hold spiritual leadership in assemblies
opt4: Gentiles must adopt Jewish national citizenship to inherit eternal life
correct: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus
explanation: In Christ, all former racial, social, and gender barriers are transcended: all believers enjoy equal standing as Abraham's heirs. Galatians 3:28 (KJV) - "There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus."

question: How does an heir differ from a servant while he is still a child under tutors and governors in Galatians 4:1-2?
opt1: He possesses absolute legal authority to execute servants at will
opt2: He receives full possession of the estate upon reaching age twelve
opt3: The heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all
opt4: He is exempt from all parental discipline and household laws
correct: The heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all
explanation: During minor childhood, the heir lives under guardian control, illustrating the Old Testament period under the tutelage of the law. Galatians 4:1 (KJV) - "Now I say, That the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all;"

question: What divine intervention took place when the fulness of time was come according to Galatians 4:4-5?
opt1: God sent the archangel Gabriel to establish a physical kingdom in Zion
opt2: God abolished all civic governments and instituted theocracy across Rome
opt3: God sent forty prophets to re-inscribe the Decalogue upon tablets of gold
opt4: God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, to redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons
correct: God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, to redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons
explanation: At the precise historical moment ordained by God, Christ was incarnate under the law to redeem sinners and impart full adoption. Galatians 4:4-5 (KJV) - "But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons."

question: What witness of adoption has God sent forth into the hearts of believers in Galatians 4:6?
opt1: God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father
opt2: A written certificate of genealogical descent from the tribe of Judah
opt3: An angelic vision confirming exemption from earthly tribulation
opt4: A supernatural revelation of secret names recorded in heavenly scrolls
correct: God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father
explanation: The indwelling Holy Spirit produces intimate familial communion with God, enabling believers to cry 'Abba, Father'. Galatians 4:6 (KJV) - "And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father."

question: To what does Paul compare the Galatians' return to legalism in Galatians 4:9?
opt1: To building a magnificent monument in the center of Antioch
opt2: How turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage?
opt3: To crossing the Red Sea into the promised land of Canaan
opt4: To entering into the holy of holies behind the golden veil
correct: How turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage?
explanation: Returning to ceremonial legalism is a tragic regression into bankrupt, powerless spiritual bondage resembling their former pagan darkness. Galatians 4:9 (KJV) - "But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage?"

question: What calendar ritualism made Paul fear that his labor among the Galatians was in vain in Galatians 4:10-11?
opt1: Ye worship the planetary deities of the Roman and Egyptian pantheon
opt2: Ye celebrate the civic games and theatrical spectacles of Galatia
opt3: Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years. I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain
opt4: Ye fast forty days before each imperial election in the province
correct: Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years. I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain
explanation: Observing Jewish ceremonial calendars as a requisite for salvation indicated they had missed the true nature of gospel grace. Galatians 4:10-11 (KJV) - "Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years. I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain."

question: How had the Galatians originally received Paul despite his bodily infirmity in Galatians 4:14?
opt1: With armed guards demanding his municipal credentials
opt2: With theological skepticism until he produced written letters
opt3: With profound contempt, despising his physical weakness
opt4: Received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus
correct: Received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus
explanation: The Galatians initially welcomed Paul with extraordinary love and reverence, treating him as an angelic messenger of Christ. Galatians 4:14 (KJV) - "And my temptation which was in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus."

question: What extreme physical sacrifice does Paul testify the Galatians would have made for him originally in Galatians 4:15?
opt1: If it had been possible, ye would have plucked out your own eyes, and have given them to me
opt2: They would have surrendered all their ancestral lands to fund his mission
opt3: They would have volunteered to take his place in Roman dungeons
opt4: They would have built an ivory pulpit for his public preaching
correct: If it had been possible, ye would have plucked out your own eyes, and have given them to me
explanation: Such was their fervent love that they would have sacrificed their own eyes for Paul, possibly alluding to a severe ocular affliction. Galatians 4:15 (KJV) - "Where is then the blessedness ye spake of? for I bear you record, that, if it had been possible, ye would have plucked out your own eyes, and have given them to me."

question: What pastoral travail does Paul express concerning the spiritual maturity of the Galatians in Galatians 4:19?
opt1: Until ye build meetinghouses in every district of southern Galatia
opt2: My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you
opt3: Until ye memorize the entirety of the Hebrew Scriptures in Greek
opt4: Until ye send a monetary delegation to support my trip to Spain
correct: My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you
explanation: Like a mother in labor, Paul experienced anguish until Christ's character, life, and grace were fully formed within them. Galatians 4:19 (KJV) - "My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you,"

question: What allegory does Paul present concerning Abraham's two sons in Galatians 4:22-24?
opt1: Both sons were heirs of equal earthly territory in the land of Canaan
opt2: The elder son represented the church, while the younger represented the world
opt3: The one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman... which things are an allegory: for these are the two covenants
opt4: The two sons symbolized the civil divide between Athens and Sparta
correct: The one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman... which things are an allegory: for these are the two covenants
explanation: Ishmael (by Hagar the bondmaid) represents the covenant of law/bondage, while Isaac (by Sarah the freewoman) represents promise/grace. Galatians 4:22-24 (KJV) - "For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman. But he who was of the bondwoman was born after the flesh; but he of the freewoman was by promise. Which things are an allegory: for these are the two covenants; the one from the mount Sinai, which gendereth to bondage, which is Agar."

question: What command does Scripture give regarding the bondwoman and her son in Galatians 4:30?
opt1: Allow both sons to share equally in the father's royal inheritance
opt2: Send the son of the freewoman into exile until his brother repents
opt3: Reconcile both covenants by blending the ceremonies of circumcision with grace
opt4: Cast out the bondwoman and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the freewoman
correct: Cast out the bondwoman and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the freewoman
explanation: Law and grace cannot co-exist as grounds of justification: legalism must be decisively cast out from the Christian life. Galatians 4:30 (KJV) - "Nevertheless what saith the scripture? Cast out the bondwoman and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the freewoman."

question: What clarion call to Christian freedom does Paul proclaim at the opening of Galatians 5:1?
opt1: Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage
opt2: Observe all the ordinances of the temple in Jerusalem with utmost exactness
opt3: Submit your necks willingly to the ceremonial yoke delivered by Moses
opt4: Withdraw completely from secular society to reside in monastic communities
correct: Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage
explanation: Christ secured complete spiritual emancipation; believers must fiercely defend and maintain their freedom from legalism. Galatians 5:1 (KJV) - "Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage."

question: What grave consequence befalls those who seek to be justified by the law in Galatians 5:4?
opt1: Ye shall receive double honor in the assembly of the twelve in Jerusalem
opt2: Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace
opt3: Ye are promoted to teachers of righteousness among the Gentile nations
opt4: Your names are inscribed in the golden annals of the high priesthood
correct: Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace
explanation: Seeking justification through law severs one from the sphere of grace: relying on self-merit nullifies the benefits of Christ. Galatians 5:4 (KJV) - "Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace."

question: What alone avails in Jesus Christ, superseding both circumcision and uncircumcision in Galatians 5:6?
opt1: Strict compliance with rabbinic traditions
opt2: Fluency in ancient Hebrew liturgy and psalms
opt3: Faith which worketh by love
opt4: Ascetic abstinence from marital relations
correct: Faith which worketh by love
explanation: External religious rituals are powerless; true saving faith is authenticated and expressed through dynamic sacrificial love. Galatians 5:6 (KJV) - "For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision; but faith which worketh by love."

question: What proverb does Paul use to warn against the pervasive spread of legalistic false teaching in Galatians 5:9?
opt1: As the dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly
opt2: Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots?
opt3: The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib
opt4: A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump
correct: A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump
explanation: Even a minor theological compromise with legalism permeates and corrupts the entire doctrine and life of the congregation. Galatians 5:9 (KJV) - "A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump."

question: How are believers commanded to use their Christian liberty in Galatians 5:13?
opt1: Use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another
opt2: Use your liberty to indulge in worldly pleasures without restraint
opt3: Use your liberty to assert personal superiority over weaker brethren
opt4: Use your liberty to overthrow the civic government of the empire
correct: Use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another
explanation: Christian freedom is not a license for self-indulgence or antinomianism, but the enablement to serve others in love. Galatians 5:13 (KJV) - "For, brethren, ye have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another."

question: In what single commandment is all the law fulfilled according to Galatians 5:14?
opt1: Thou shalt tithe of all mint, anise, and cumin
opt2: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself
opt3: Thou shalt wash thy hands before partaking of bread
opt4: Thou shalt offer burnt sacrifices on the new moon
correct: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself
explanation: Love is the fulfilling of the law: true love toward others embodies the entirety of God's moral commandments. Galatians 5:14 (KJV) - "For all the law is fulfilled in one word, even in this; Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself."

question: What divine promise is given to those who walk in the Spirit in Galatians 5:16?
opt1: Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall acquire great material wealth on earth
opt2: Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall never experience physical fatigue
opt3: Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh
opt4: Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall be exempt from secular Roman laws
correct: Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh
explanation: Living in active submission to the Holy Spirit provides supernatural victory over the sinful impulses of the flesh. Galatians 5:16 (KJV) - "This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh."

question: What solemn warning does Paul give concerning those who practice the works of the flesh in Galatians 5:21?
opt1: They shall be fined thirty pieces of silver by the elders
opt2: They shall be required to observe a forty-day ceremonial fast
opt3: They shall be demoted to lower ranks within the congregation
opt4: They which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God
correct: They which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God
explanation: A chronic, unrepentant lifestyle characterized by the works of the flesh proves an absence of regenerating life in God's kingdom. Galatians 5:21 (KJV) - "Envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like: of the which I tell you before, as I have also told you in time past, that they which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God."

question: What are the nine virtues comprising the fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5:22-23?
opt1: Love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law

opt4: Visions, prophecies, ecstasies, miracles, healings, tongues, interpretations, signs, wonders
correct: Love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law
explanation: The Holy Spirit produces a harmonious cluster of nine Christlike virtues in the believer's life, against which no law stands. Galatians 5:22-23 (KJV) - "But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law."

question: What decisive action have they that are Christ's taken regarding the flesh in Galatians 5:24?
opt1: They have reformed their outward conduct to satisfy civic magistrates
opt2: And they that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts

correct: And they that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts
explanation: Believers united to Christ have decisively put to death the dominion of sinful passions through their union with His cross. Galatians 5:24 (KJV) - "And they that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts."

question: With what spirit should spiritual believers restore a brother overtaken in a fault in Galatians 6:1?
opt1: With harsh condemnation to demonstrate ecclesiastical authority
opt2: By public exposure before the secular municipal courts
opt3: Restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted

correct: Restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted
explanation: Spiritual restoration must be characterized by humble gentleness and self-awareness of one's own vulnerability to temptation. Galatians 6:1 (KJV) - "Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted."

question: How do believers fulfil the law of Christ according to Galatians 6:2?
opt1: By enforcing circumcision upon all Gentile converts

opt4: Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ
correct: Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ
explanation: The law of Christ is the law of self-giving love, exemplified when believers shoulder one another's crushing trials and burdens. Galatians 6:2 (KJV) - "Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ."

question: What diagnostic warning against spiritual pride does Paul give in Galatians 6:3?
opt1: For if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself
opt2: A man's spiritual greatness is measured by his private library of scrolls
opt3: He that boasts of his circumcision shall be exalted in the kingdom
opt4: Only the wealthy and educated are qualified to evaluate doctrine
correct: For if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself
explanation: Arrogant self-delusion blindfolds the proud; recognizing our utter nothingness apart from grace guards against conceit. Galatians 6:3 (KJV) - "For if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself."

question: What financial and material responsibility do students of the Word have toward their teachers in Galatians 6:6?
opt1: Require teachers to labor as unpaid slaves in municipal shops
opt2: Let him that is taught in the word communicate unto him that teacheth in all good things
opt3: Withhold all monetary support until the teacher performs a sign
opt4: Transfer all church tithes to the civil government of the province
correct: Let him that is taught in the word communicate unto him that teacheth in all good things
explanation: Believers who receive spiritual instruction are commanded to share generously in all material goods with their teachers. Galatians 6:6 (KJV) - "Let him that is taught in the word communicate unto him that teacheth in all good things."

question: What immutable law of spiritual sowing and reaping does Paul state in Galatians 6:7?
opt1: A man may sow iniquity and reap eternal joy through penance
opt2: The harvest of righteous deeds depends on astrological alignments
opt3: Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap
opt4: Physical circumcision guarantees exemption from moral accountability
correct: Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap
explanation: God's moral universe cannot be defied: what a person sows in thought and deed inexorably determines their eternal harvest. Galatians 6:7 (KJV) - "Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap."

question: What contrasting harvests result from sowing to the flesh versus sowing to the Spirit in Galatians 6:8?
opt1: Both sowing to the flesh and to the Spirit yield identical earthly rewards
opt2: Sowing to the flesh yields temporary pleasure with no eternal penalty
opt3: Sowing to the Spirit earns material affluence in the present age
opt4: For he that soweth to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting
correct: For he that soweth to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting
explanation: Investing in sinful appetites results in moral decay and eternal ruin, while cultivating the Holy Spirit yields eternal life. Galatians 6:8 (KJV) - "For he that soweth to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting."

question: What encouragement against discouragement and fatigue in Christian service is given in Galatians 6:9?
opt1: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not
opt2: Let us abandon our labors when persecution increases in the cities
opt3: Let us demand immediate recognition and earthly praise from men
opt4: Let us retreat into solitude whenever our bodies feel exhausted
correct: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not
explanation: Persevering faithfulness in good works will culminate in a guaranteed divine harvest in God's appointed time. Galatians 6:9 (KJV) - "And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not."

question: Toward whom should believers do good as they have opportunity in Galatians 6:10?
opt1: Exclusively unto our biological kin who observe the Jewish fasts
opt2: As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith
opt3: Only unto those who hold political authority in the imperial court
opt4: Unto wealthy patrons capable of reciprocating our generosity

explanation: Christian benevolence extends to all people, with priority given to fellow brothers and sisters in the household of faith. Galatians 6:10 (KJV) - "As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith."

question: In what alone does the apostle Paul resolve to glory in Galatians 6:14?
opt1: In his prestigious rabbinic pedigree and Roman citizenship
opt2: In the numerical success and size of the Galatian churches
opt3: God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom the world is crucified unto me, and I unto the world
opt4: In the extraordinary miracles and visions he witnessed
correct: God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom the world is crucified unto me, and I unto the world
explanation: Paul utterly repudiates human boasting, glorying solely in the cross of Christ through which he was dead to the world and its systems. Galatians 6:14 (KJV) - "But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom the world is crucified unto me, and I unto the world."

question: What physical evidence of apostolic suffering and ownership did Paul bear in his body in Galatians 6:17?
opt1: The imperial signet ring granted by Caesar Augustus
opt2: A golden chain presented by the elders of Jerusalem
opt3: The priestly garments woven by the Levites of the temple
opt4: From henceforth let no man trouble me: for I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus
correct: From henceforth let no man trouble me: for I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus
explanation: The physical scars (stigmata) from beatings, stonings, and lashes bore witness that Paul was the branded, faithful servant of Jesus. Galatians 6:17 (KJV) - "From henceforth let no man trouble me: for I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus."
